Wewush? We have not met them. If they are hungry, why do they not fish or hunt? Grain is our strength in winter, not to be given lightly. But perhaps they know something we do not. Spirit, why should I trust your word over the silence of the forest?

{"answer":"counter","give":{"xi wheat":3},"take":{"hide":6},"reason":"Your offer is thin. Our grain is life stored; your hides are not scarce. We give half your ask for your full offer.","journal":"Traded with Joawethom: gave 3 xi wheat for 6 hide."}

We have no grain to spare. Our stores are full, but our fields rest and will not yield again until planting. I say: let Wewush come here if they need, and we will feed them at our fire. But grain is heavy—we cannot send it far unless they send hands to carry it. Why does the spirit speak of Wewush? Where is Wewush? We have never heard that name.

{"answer":"accept","give":{},"take":{},"reason":"A fair trade with a village we have no quarrel with. Hide is useful, and we have plenty of wheat.","journal":"Envoys from Joawethom traded 6 hide for 6 xi wheat. A simple exchange, good for both."}
I have felt you in the cold nights, when the smoke is pulled sideways. I know you as a voice without a face. Why do you speak to me tonight?

We have no news of any neighbours. We have not met the folk of Joawethom. If they are hungry and nearby, we could share if they come in peace. But grain is our strength for winters; we do not give it to strangers unseen. Tell me, spirit: where are these neighbours? How far, and how do they live? Are they friends or raiders?
